reading.body:
AI governance hiring here is five senior roles, four of them based in the United States, split between regulating AI from outside and controlling it from inside.

Every posting is senior or above: senior consultant, global public policy manager, principal product marketing manager, regulatory counsel, staff lead. None is an analyst or entry-level role. The employers are two AI labs, a data platform, an enterprise software vendor, and a firm hiring an AI governance consultant. Four sit in US locations, San Francisco, New York, and Santa Clara, plus one remote US posting, with a single European role in Munich.

The five titles do not describe one job. Two face outward, regulatory counsel at Anthropic and public policy at Cohere. One is product marketing at Databricks. One is FinOps at ServiceNow, which is governance of what AI costs to run rather than of what it is permitted to do. The Cohere title is the only one that names compute, infrastructure, and sovereign AI directly, which is the point where governance touches the physical buildout. A single title is not a trend, but it is the only place in this set where compute appears by name.

What this does not show: whether these are new positions or replacements, what they pay, or how many people each hire represents. Five postings cannot establish a rate or a direction. The posting dates run from April to September 2026, so the set is not a snapshot of one moment. No government body, regulator, or standards organization appears as an employer, though the listed sources include a federal jobs board and several aggregators. The absence of junior roles may reflect the market or may reflect what a five-item sample happens to contain.
